iconicAnchor.label: Nineteenth-century Gothic Revival design
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: British and international Gothic Revival movement
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Revival architecture and designed objects establish pointed structure, vertical rhythm, tracery, material craft, and moral-historical intent as a coordinated design language.

sources.title: The Gothic style – an introduction
supports: Gothic Revival drew on medieval pointed construction, tracery, carving, and vertical emphasis across architecture and decorative arts.

sources.title: Stained glass: Gothic Revival and beyond
supports: Revival stained glass demonstrates how colored transmitted light, lead structure, figure, and architectural framing produce atmosphere and hierarchy.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches ornate, axial, medieval, shadow heavy, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/gothic-revival/reference-01.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
